questions.id: What is the negation of (A AND B)?
questions.stem:
(A) NOT A OR NOT B
(B) NOT A AND NOT B
(C) NOT A OR B
(D) A AND NOT B
questions.solution: De Morgan's law states that the negation of a conjunction (AND) is equivalent to the disjunction (OR) of the negations. So, the negation of (A AND B) is (NOT A OR NOT B).
questions.explanation: De Morgan's laws help simplify logical expressions by negating both the operands and the operator.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing (C) which is the negation of only one operand. Remember, De Morgan's law applies to both operands.

questions.id: What is the negation of (A OR B AND C)?
questions.stem:
(A) NOT A AND NOT (B AND C)
(B) NOT A OR NOT B AND NOT C
(C) NOT A AND NOT B OR NOT C
(D) NOT (A OR B) AND NOT C

choices.A: NOT A AND NOT (B AND C)
choices.B: NOT A OR NOT B AND NOT C
choices.C: NOT A AND NOT B OR NOT C
choices.D: NOT (A OR B) AND NOT C

questions.solution: De Morgan's law can be applied to multiple operands as well. The negation of (A OR B AND C) is (NOT A AND NOT B) AND (NOT A AND NOT C), which simplifies to NOT (A OR B) AND NOT C.
questions.explanation: When applying De Morgan's laws, consider the grouping and apply the law to each group separately.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing (B) or (C) by incorrectly distributing the negation. Remember to apply De Morgan's law to the entire expression within parentheses.

questions.id: What is the negation of ((NOT A) OR B)?
questions.stem:
(A) A AND NOT B
(B) A OR NOT B
(C) NOT (NOT A) AND B
(D) NOT (NOT A OR B)
questions.solution: The negation of ((NOT A) OR B) is NOT (NOT A OR B), which simplifies to (A AND NOT B).
questions.explanation: When applying De Morgan's laws, remember that NOT distributes over OR and AND.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing (C) by reversing the operands without negating them. Remember to negate both the operands and the operator.
